3. Median stay by state and diagnosis

Rows are ordered by overall median, shortest at the top. Three things the grid shows that a single combined map could not:

  • The geography is not the same for every diagnosis. Psychosis and behavioral run long in a different set of states than substance use does, so any single mental health map averages away real variation.
  • Psychosis is both the longest row and the widest, with far more spread between states than the other diagnoses — it would dominate any combined measure.
  • Eating disorders is mostly grey, and behavioral is patchy in the sparser states. Those two rows should not be read as geographic patterns; they are closer to a map of where Epic’s footprint is large enough to clear the suppression threshold.
